repo.description: LangChain4j is an idiomatic, open-source Java library for building LLM-powered applications on the JVM. It offers a unified API over popular LLM providers and vector stores, and makes implementing tool calling (including MCP support), agents and RAG easy. It integrates seamlessly with enterprise Java frameworks like Quarkus and Spring Boot.

body:
## Issue
No issue. Follow-up to #6420.

## Change
The proxy, the validation and the tool error notice each decided for themselves which methods of an AI Service interface are implemented by calling the model. As a result, the tool error notice had to know about `ChatMemoryAccess`.

`AiServiceValidation.isImplementedByModel(Method)` is now the only place that decides this:
- static and default methods run as written;
- `Object` and `ChatMemoryAccess` methods are handled by the proxy itself;
- every other method calls the model.

What changes as a result:
- **Proxy (`DefaultAiServices`)**: methods that do not call the model go to `invokeImplementedByProxy()`. The dispatch is the same as before.
- **Validation**: return-type checks are no longer applied to `getChatMemory()` and `evictChatMemory()` as if they were AI Service methods. Until now they passed only because `dev.langchain4j.memory.` is not in `LANGCHAIN4J_PACKAGES`. Adding it there would have broken every AI Service that extends `ChatMemoryAccess`.
- **`ToolErrorHandlingNotice`**: it no longer inspects methods. `DefaultAiServices` supplies a `BooleanSupplier` that says whether any method returns neither an asynchronous nor a reactive type. The notice calls it only when the AI Service has tools, as before.

Everything touched is package-private or private. There is no change to the public API or to behaviour.

Tests:
- `AiServiceValidationTest`: an interface with a static method returning a LangChain4j type, and an AI Service extending `ChatMemoryAccess`. Each fails if the corresponding rule is removed.
- `AiServicesTest`: `getChatMemory()` and `evictChatMemory()` called through the proxy, with both existing and missing memories, without calling the model.
- `ToolErrorHandlingNoticeTest` uses the real `DefaultAiServices.hasBlockingMethod()` instead of a copy of the predicate.

## General checklist
- [X] There are no breaking changes (API, behaviour)
- [X] I have added unit and/or integration tests for my change
- [X] The tests cover both positive and negative cases
- [X] I have manually run all the unit and integration tests in the module I have added/changed, and they are all green
- [ ] I have manually run all the unit and integration tests in the [core](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j/tree/main/langchain4j-core) and [main](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j/tree/main/langchain4j) modules, and they are all green
- [ ] I have added/updated the [documentation](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j/tree/main/docs/docs)
- [ ] I have added an example in the [examples repo](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j-examples) (only for "big" features)
- [ ] I have added/updated [Spring Boot starter(s)](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j-spring) (if applicable)
